metadata.title: Standard PCR (Endpoint DNA Amplification with Taq DNA Polymerase)
metadata.purpose: Amplify a specific DNA target from a template by endpoint PCR using Taq DNA polymerase with Standard Taq Buffer, producing a double-stranded amplicon for downstream analysis (e.g. agarose gel electrophoresis, cloning, sequencing).
metadata.scope: Routine endpoint PCR with wild-type Taq DNA Polymerase (NEB #M0273) and Standard Taq Reaction Buffer for targets up to ~5 kb. Not intended for high-fidelity, long-range (>5 kb), quantitative (qPCR), or GC-rich templates that require a proofreading or hot-start enzyme.
beforeYouBegin: Design forward and reverse primers flanking the target; know the amplicon length (to set extension time at 1 min/kb) and primer Tm (to set the annealing temperature).
Assemble all reaction components on ice; keep Taq DNA Polymerase in a cooling block.
Preheat the thermal cycler to the 95 C denaturation temperature before loading tubes.

materials.name: 10X Standard Taq Reaction Buffer
materials.specification: 10X concentrate; 1X = 10 mM Tris-HCl, 50 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2, pH 8.3 at 25 C (standard NEB formulation; exact composition not stated on the fetched protocol page)

materials.name: Deoxynucleotide (dNTP) solution mix
materials.specification: 10 mM each of dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP

materials.name: Forward primer
materials.specification: 10 uM stock; sequence is target-specific and defined by the user
materials.rawText: 10 uM Forward Primer  1 uL  0.2 uM (0.05-1 uM)

materials.name: Reverse primer
materials.specification: 10 uM stock; sequence is target-specific and defined by the user
materials.rawText: 10 uM Reverse Primer  1 uL  0.2 uM (0.05-1 uM)

materials.name: Taq DNA Polymerase
materials.rawText: Taq DNA Polymerase  0.25 uL  1.25 Units/50 uL PCR

materials.name: Nuclease-free water
materials.specification: Molecular-biology grade; brings reaction to final volume

equipment.name: Programmable thermal cycler
equipment.settings: Preheat block to 95 C (denaturation temperature) before loading; heated lid enabled

samples.name: Template DNA
samples.description: Genomic, plasmid, or cDNA template; use < 1000 ng per 50 uL reaction. Organism/source is defined by the user.

samples.name: PCR amplicon
samples.description: Double-stranded DNA product spanning the primer-defined target region; length is target-dependent.

tables.title: PCR reaction setup (master mix)
tables.note: Assemble on ice. For multiple reactions, prepare a template-free master mix and aliquot, then add template.

tables.title: Thermocycling program
tables.note: The denaturation/annealing/extension trio is repeated for 30 cycles. Set the annealing temperature to the primer Tm (guidance range 45-68 C); set extension time to ~1 min per kb of amplicon.

steps.action: Thaw and gently mix all reagents; keep on ice throughout assembly.
steps.criticalNotes: Add the polymerase last and keep it in a cooling block.

steps.action: Assemble the PCR reaction in a thin-walled PCR tube on ice per the master-mix table (scale to 25 uL or 50 uL).
steps.expectedResult: Complete reaction mix, template plus primers, ready to cycle.

steps.action: Gently mix the reaction, briefly spin down, and transfer tubes to the thermal cycler preheated to 95 C.
Run the thermocycling program: initial denaturation, then 30 cycles of denaturation/annealing/extension, followed by a final extension and hold.
steps.expectedResult: Exponential accumulation of the target amplicon.

steps.action: Hold the reaction at 4-10 C; analyze an aliquot by agarose gel electrophoresis or proceed to downstream use, or store.
steps.expectedResult: A single band of the expected size on an agarose gel.

controls.name: NTC (no-template control)
controls.description: Reaction with nuclease-free water in place of template DNA to detect reagent/primer contamination. Recommended good practice; not specified on the source protocol page.

controls.name: Positive control template
controls.description: A template known to amplify with the primer pair, to confirm reagents and cycling performed correctly.

expectedOutputs: A discrete double-stranded DNA band of the expected amplicon size on an agarose gel.
No product in the no-template control.

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing temperature too high; too little template; degraded primers/enzyme
troubleshooting.solution: Lower annealing temperature toward primer Tm; increase template (<1000 ng); use fresh primers/Taq

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing temperature too low; excess primer or template; too many cycles
troubleshooting.solution: Raise annealing temperature; reduce primer/template; reduce cycle number

troubleshooting.cause: Extension too long or too much enzyme/template
troubleshooting.solution: Shorten extension; reduce Taq and template amounts

safety: Wear gloves and eye protection; follow institutional rules for handling and disposing of PCR reagents and, downstream, any DNA stain used for gel visualization.
limitations: Wild-type Taq lacks 3'->5' proofreading, so this protocol is not appropriate where high fidelity is required. Amplicon length, annealing temperature, and extension time must be tuned to the specific primer pair and target and are left to the user.
